parameters.content:
## 10 Error Handler (shared)

Catches failures from the other workflows and writes them onto the affected Event as an External Integration Log entry, so the coordinator sees failures where they already see responses.

### How it finds the event
The error trigger payload never carries the failing workflow's data, so **Fetch Failed Execution** reads the execution through the n8n API and looks for an event ID in the nodes listed in `EVENT_ID_NODES`.

### Setup
1. Administrate OAuth2 credential on **Log Failure**.
2. n8n API credential on **Fetch Failed Execution** (same project as this workflow).
3. Set this as the **Error Workflow** in the settings of 30, 40, 50, 60 and 70.
4. Activate.

Error workflows fire on production runs only, never on manual runs.

## Config

**ORIGIN_IDENTIFIER** - label for log entries. Keep it identical in every workflow.

**TRANSIENT_MARKERS** - comma separated text that marks a failure as temporary.

**N8N_API_URL** - `https://YOUR-N8N-HOST/api/v1`.

**EVENT_ID_NODES** / **EVENT_ID_FIELDS** - where to look for the event ID in the failed run. Update if you rename those nodes.

nodes.name: Fetch Failed Execution
nodes.notes:
Needs a credential. Choose an n8n API credential that belongs to the same n8n project as this workflow. Without it this node fails harmlessly, the handler takes the Done branch and the failure stays in the n8n execution list.

Why this node exists: the error trigger payload never carries the failing workflow's data. The failed execution does, so it is fetched here to recover the event ID.
